chapter_summary: Proverbs 11 is a gallery of contrasts: honest versus dishonest, proud versus humble, generous versus greedy, righteous versus wicked. Every pairing teaches the same underlying truth — God sees all things, and He rewards those who walk uprightly while allowing the wicked to be destroyed by their own choices. The chapter also emphasises that righteousness is not private — it affects families, cities, and whole communities. Generosity is shown to multiply, while hoarding leads to loss. The chapter closes with the reminder that both the righteous and the wicked will receive what they deserve.
main_lesson: God loves honesty, humility, and generosity — and He blesses those who live that way.

memory_verse.kjv: When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
memory_verse.little_bible: Pride brings shame. But the humble person gains wisdom.

parent_guide: Proverbs 11 continues Solomon's antithetic proverbs — each verse holds two opposite paths side by side. This structure is ideal for children: they naturally understand fairness, comparison, and consequences. As you read each proverb, ask your child to predict what the second half will say after hearing the first. The chapter covers cheating in business (v.1), pride (v.2), integrity (v.3), the uselessness of wealth at death (v.4), generosity (vv.24-26), and community wellbeing (vv.10-11). These themes open rich conversations about character, money, words, and legacy. Verse 30 ('he that winneth souls is wise') is an evangelism prompt — a wonderful opportunity to introduce the idea that caring about other people's relationship with God is itself wisdom. Remind children that all of these proverbs are not rules to earn God's love, but wisdom for a good life, given by a God who loves them.
application_for_children: This week, practise one act of honesty and one act of generosity every day. Notice how it feels — and watch what God does.

verses.kjv: A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight.
verses.little_bible: God hates cheating. He loves honest dealing. Cheating in any trade is an abomination to Him. But fair and honest measures bring Him delight.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God hates cheating. He loves being fair.
verses.meaning: A 'false balance' was a dishonest set of scales used to cheat buyers. God declares such cheating an abomination — the strongest language of disgust in the Old Testament. Honesty in all dealings is not merely polite; it reflects God's own character.
verses.prayer: God, help me always be honest and fair.
verses.discussion_question: Why does cheating make God angry?
verses.family_discussion: Where might subtle dishonesty creep into daily life — pricing, reporting, marking — and how do we model and cultivate integrity at home?
verses.do_it_today: Find one chance to be completely honest today, even when no one is watching.
verses.illustration_prompt: A market stall with two scales: one tipped dishonestly with a frown, one perfectly balanced with a golden glow, watercolour style with warm earthy tones

verses.kjv: When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
verses.little_bible: Pride always leads to shame. Humility is where wisdom lives. The person who thinks too highly of themselves will fall. But the humble one keeps growing in wisdom.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride leads to shame. Humility finds wisdom.
verses.meaning: Pride is the elevation of self above God and others — and it reliably precedes disgrace. Lowliness (humility) is the posture that allows wisdom to take root, because the humble person remains teachable.
verses.prayer: God, help me stay humble and teachable.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when someone always thinks they are best?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate genuine humility in our home — not low self-esteem, but accurate, God-centred self-understanding?
verses.do_it_today: Let someone else go first today. Let them have the best seat, the first turn, the biggest piece.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child puffed up proudly stumbling and falling, while a small humble child beside them is given a crown of flowers, watercolour gentle contrast

verses.kjv: The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.
verses.little_bible: Living with integrity guides you on the right path. But disobeying God and twisting the truth will destroy you. Good character leads you safely forward.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Integrity guides you. Doing wrong destroys you.
verses.meaning: Integrity — consistent honesty and uprightness — functions as an internal compass. It guides the upright even when no external rule applies. But those who twist truth and disobey God destroy themselves with their own choices.
verses.prayer: God, make me a person of integrity.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be honest even when it is hard?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children that integrity is not just rule-following but a whole way of being — in heart, word, and action?
verses.do_it_today: Do the right thing today even when no one is watching and it costs you something.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking confidently on a clear lit path guided by glowing footsteps, while another path crumbles into darkness, soft watercolour landscape

verses.kjv: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.
verses.little_bible: Money and riches cannot save you when God judges. Only righteousness can deliver you from death. On your most important day, only how you lived before God matters.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Riches cannot save you. Righteousness can.
verses.meaning: When God's judgment comes, wealth offers no protection. Righteousness — right standing before God — is the only thing that delivers from death. This is ultimately a Gospel pointer: only the righteousness of Christ can truly save.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You, not riches.
verses.discussion_question: What matters more: money or a good heart?
verses.family_discussion: How do we free our children from trusting in wealth or status, and instead ground their security in God's righteousness?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God for something that money could never buy — love, forgiveness, peace, or life itself.
verses.illustration_prompt: A treasure chest left behind in darkness while a glowing figure walks forward into light, watercolour with warm contrast of shadow and radiance

verses.kjv: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
verses.little_bible: The person who lives rightly will have their path directed by God. But the wicked person will be tripped up and fall by their own wrong choices.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Right living directs your path. Wrong choices make you fall.
verses.meaning: 'Perfect' here means wholehearted, not sinless — a person fully devoted to God. Their righteousness becomes a guide that directs their path. The wicked, however, are undone not by some outside force but by the natural consequences of their own wickedness.
verses.prayer: God, direct my path by Your righteousness.
verses.discussion_question: How do our choices make our path easier or harder?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand that consequences are often built into choices — not just punishment imposed from outside?
verses.do_it_today: Before you choose something today, ask: will this make my path easier or harder?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking a straight sunny road that bends gently forward, while a figure in shadows trips and falls on a twisted rocky path, watercolour style

verses.kjv: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them: but transgressors shall be taken in their own naughtiness.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person is delivered — rescued — by their own upright living. But those who keep disobeying God get caught in their own doing wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Doing right rescues you. Doing wrong traps you.
verses.meaning: Righteousness acts as a kind of rescue — it protects and delivers those who walk in it. Those who disobey God, however, are caught by the very trap they set through their own wrongdoing.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from traps of my own making.
verses.discussion_question: Has doing the right thing ever kept you out of trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children see that honesty and obedience often protect them in ways they cannot fully see at the time?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to do the right thing in one situation today and watch how it protects you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child stepping safely over a hidden snare on the path, bathed in warm light, while a shadowy figure is caught in a trap below, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust men perisheth.
verses.little_bible: When a wicked person dies, every hope they had dies with them. Their plans and wishes all come to nothing. Only those who trust God have real hope beyond death.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wicked person's hopes all die with them.
verses.meaning: The wicked build their hope on things that end at death — wealth, power, reputation, plans. When they die, all of it perishes. Only hope rooted in God and righteousness transcends death.
verses.prayer: God, let my hope be rooted in You.
verses.discussion_question: What is one hope that would last even beyond this life?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate an eternal perspective in our children — building hope in God rather than in things that pass away?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing you hope for that will last forever. Thank God for that hope.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crumbling castle of gold turning to dust in shadow, while a single candle burns brightly in a window with a cross silhouette, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.
verses.little_bible: God delivers the righteous person out of trouble. And the wicked person steps into that same trouble in their place. God's protection on the righteous is real.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God rescues the righteous from trouble.
verses.meaning: God's providential care for the righteous means He extracts them from danger and distress. In a striking twist, the wicked end up in the very trouble from which the righteous were rescued — their own schemes often become their prison.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for delivering me from trouble.
verses.discussion_question: Can you remember a time God helped you out of a hard situation?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate gratitude and recognition of God's protective hand in our family's story?
verses.do_it_today: Tell your family about one time God helped your family out of a hard situation.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child being lifted safely out of a deep pit by glowing hands while darkness below remains, warm rescue-scene watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: An hypocrite with his mouth destroyeth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the just be delivered.
verses.little_bible: A hypocrite uses words to hurt and destroy the people around them. But the just person — who knows truth — is protected. Words have great power to harm or to save.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hurtful words destroy. Truth and justice protect.
verses.meaning: A hypocrite uses speech to destroy — spreading lies and flattery that ruin reputations. Knowledge (of truth and of God's ways) equips the just person to avoid and overcome such destruction. Wisdom in words is protective.
verses.prayer: God, guard my words and keep me from lying.
verses.discussion_question: How can words hurt someone even without touching them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children to speak truthfully even when a lie would be easier — and to recognise when words are being used to harm?
verses.do_it_today: Say something kind and true to one person today. Let your words build rather than tear down.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child's words shown as glowing golden birds flying upward, beside a shadow figure whose dark words break a friend's image, watercolour split-scene

verses.kjv: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.
verses.little_bible: When good and righteous people do well, the whole city is happy! And when wicked people are removed from power, people shout with relief. Righteousness blesses everyone around it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteousness blesses the whole city.
verses.meaning: Righteousness is not private — it has communal effects. When good people prosper and lead, the whole community benefits and rejoices. The destruction of wickedness is also cause for relief and celebration by the oppressed.
verses.prayer: God, make me a blessing to those around me.
verses.discussion_question: How does one good person make things better for everyone around them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we raise children who understand that their character choices affect not just themselves but their families, schools, and communities?
verses.do_it_today: Do something good for your street or neighbourhood this week — pick up litter, greet a neighbour, help someone.
verses.illustration_prompt: A joyful town square with people celebrating and colourful bunting, bright sunlight pouring down, warm community watercolour scene

verses.kjv: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
verses.little_bible: The blessing that comes through upright people lifts a whole city up. But the wicked person's words can tear a whole city down. Character shapes communities.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people lift their city up. Wicked words tear it down.
verses.meaning: Cities and communities are elevated or destroyed not primarily by economics or politics but by the moral character of their people and leaders. The blessing of the upright is generative; the speech of the wicked is destructive.
verses.prayer: God, help me be a blessing wherever I am.
verses.discussion_question: How can even one person's good words help a whole group of people?
verses.family_discussion: What does it mean to be a community-builder rather than a community-destroyer — at school, in your street, in your church?
verses.do_it_today: Say something encouraging to someone today that lifts them up rather than tearing them down.
verses.illustration_prompt: A city on a hill glowing in warm sunlight, with an upright family figure at the gate smiling outward, gentle community watercolour landscape

verses.kjv: He that is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holdeth his peace.
verses.little_bible: A foolish person looks down on and despises those around them. But a wise person with understanding knows when to stay quiet. Wisdom speaks carefully — or not at all.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Foolish people despise others. Wise people stay calm.
verses.meaning: Contempt for neighbours is a mark of folly — it reveals a self-centred, proud heart. The person of understanding, however, exercises restraint. They do not voice every criticism or negative thought — wisdom includes knowing when silence is best.
verses.prayer: God, help me be kind and slow to judge others.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wise to think before you speak?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model and teach the discipline of holding our peace — not every thought needs to be spoken, especially harsh or dismissive ones?
verses.do_it_today: Before you say something critical today, stop and ask: is this kind, true, and necessary?
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise child sitting quietly and peacefully while another child speaks unkindly beside them, warm afternoon watercolour with gentle contrast

verses.kjv: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.
verses.little_bible: A person who gossips shares secrets that were never theirs to tell. But a faithful, trustworthy person keeps a secret safe. Being trustworthy with private things is a mark of true friendship.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A gossip shares secrets. A faithful friend keeps them.
verses.meaning: The talebearer (gossip) cannot be trusted — they will share what was told in confidence. But a person of faithful spirit is a safe harbour for private information. Faithfulness in this area builds deep trust.
verses.prayer: God, make me a trustworthy and faithful friend.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to keep a friend's secret?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children the difference between sharing information helpfully and spreading gossip — where is the line?
verses.do_it_today: If someone has trusted you with a private thing, keep it today. Do not share it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child cupping their hands protectively around a glowing secret, a faithful expression on their face, watercolour warm-toned friendship scene

verses.kjv: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
verses.little_bible: When people refuse to listen to wise advice, things go wrong. But when many wise people give their counsel together, there is safety in that. Never think you already know everything.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many wise advisors bring safety.
verses.meaning: Wisdom is rarely a solo pursuit. Those who reject counsel and trust only themselves fall. Safety — in decisions, in leadership, in life — comes from seeking and accepting input from multiple wise, godly counsellors.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen to wise advice.
verses.discussion_question: Who are the wise people you should listen to?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children the habit of seeking counsel — from parents, Scripture, trusted mentors — rather than always relying on their own understanding?
verses.do_it_today: Ask one wise person in your life for advice about a decision you are facing.
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of wise elders and a child sitting together at a round table with an open book, warm golden light, watercolour advisory scene

verses.kjv: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.
verses.little_bible: If you promise to pay someone else's debts without knowing them well, you will be hurt by it. But the person who avoids risky financial promises stays safe. Be wise with your money commitments.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Be careful about promises involving money.
verses.meaning: Making oneself liable for a stranger's debts is financially reckless. The proverb warns against impulsive financial commitments — especially for unknown parties. Wisdom includes prudence about the promises and obligations we undertake.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom before I make big promises.
verses.discussion_question: Why should you think carefully before making a big promise?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children that commitments and promises have real weight — and that wisdom involves thinking through consequences before we commit?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a promise you have made. Are you keeping it? Do what you said you would do.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child pausing thoughtfully before signing a piece of paper, a wise parent hand on their shoulder, soft watercolour home scene

verses.kjv: A gracious woman retaineth honour: and strong men retain riches.
verses.little_bible: A gracious woman holds on to honour and respect through her kindness and character. Strong and diligent men hold on to the things they have worked for. Character retains what it earns.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A kind woman keeps honour. Hard workers keep what they earn.
verses.meaning: Character is the key to retaining what matters most. A woman of grace retains honour — not by force but through the quality of who she is. Diligent men retain wealth through their strength of work ethic. In both cases, character sustains.
verses.prayer: God, help me build good character every day.
verses.discussion_question: How does being kind help people respect you more?
verses.family_discussion: How do we honour both grace and diligence as household values — showing children that character and hard work, not just talent, lead to lasting things?
verses.do_it_today: Show grace to someone who is difficult to be kind to today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A kind woman with a gentle smile wearing a crown of honour, and a strong worker with calloused hands holding a basket of fruit, watercolour pair illustration

verses.kjv: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.
verses.little_bible: Being merciful and kind to others actually does good to your own soul. But cruelty and harshness harm your own life from the inside. Kindness is a gift you give yourself too.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Kindness does good to your own soul.
verses.meaning: Mercy is not just altruistic — it benefits the giver. A merciful person nourishes their own soul through acts of compassion. Conversely, cruelty corrupts the cruel person from within. The heart is shaped by what it practices.
verses.prayer: God, make me merciful and kind always.
verses.discussion_question: How does being kind to others make you feel inside?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand that the character they practise shapes who they become — kindness grows more kindness, cruelty grows more cruelty?
verses.do_it_today: Do one act of mercy today — help someone, forgive someone, or speak gently to someone who is struggling.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child helping a smaller child up from the ground, both smiling, glowing warmth radiating from them, gentle watercolour compassion scene

verses.kjv: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward.
verses.little_bible: The wicked person works hard at deception — but that work leads nowhere good. The person who sows righteousness, however, will receive a sure and certain reward from God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Sow righteousness and reap a sure reward.
verses.meaning: Deceptive labour produces false results — the wicked think they are building something, but it is all illusion. In contrast, sowing righteousness — consistently doing right — produces a certain harvest. God guarantees the reward.
verses.prayer: God, help me sow righteousness every day.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to sow righteousness like planting a seed?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand the sowing-and-reaping principle — that faithful, righteous habits are seeds that produce a real harvest in God's time?
verses.do_it_today: Plant a seed of righteousness today: one honest word, one kind act, one right choice.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child planting glowing seeds in rich soil, with small golden plants already sprouting, warm harvest sunrise in background, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: As righteousness tendeth to life: so he that pursueth evil pursueth it to his own death.
verses.little_bible: Righteousness leads to life. This is certain. But evil is a road that ends in death. Those who chase after evil are chasing their own destruction without knowing it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteousness leads to life. Evil leads to death.
verses.meaning: There are only two ultimate destinations: life and death. Righteousness is the path to life — not just physical life but the abundant, God-given life. Evil is a path that ends in death, including spiritual death and separation from God.
verses.prayer: God, keep me on the path to life.
verses.discussion_question: Why does doing wrong always lead somewhere bad in the end?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a long-view perspective — seeing that every path leads somewhere, and wisdom chooses the path that leads to life?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: is the path I am on today leading toward life or away from it?
verses.illustration_prompt: Two paths diverging: one lit and green leading upward toward a bright horizon, one dark and downward into shadow, watercolour symbolic landscape

verses.kjv: They that are of a froward heart are abomination to the LORD: but such as are upright in their way are his delight.
verses.little_bible: A twisted and disobedient heart is an abomination to God — He hates what it produces. But the person who walks uprightly before God is His delight. God cares about our hearts, not just our actions.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God hates a twisted heart. He delights in an upright one.
verses.meaning: 'Froward' means twisted or perverse — a heart set against God's ways. Such a heart is abominable to God. But the upright heart — aligned with God's truth and ways — brings Him delight. God looks at the heart first.
verses.prayer: God, make my heart upright before You.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God care about your heart first?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate heart-level discipleship in our children — not just outward behaviour compliance but a heart that genuinely loves what God loves?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to search your heart today and show you anything that is twisted or out of line with His ways.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with an open glowing heart lifted toward a radiant sky, warm golden divine light shining down, tender watercolour devotion scene

verses.kjv: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
verses.little_bible: Even if many wicked people join together and make a pact, they will not escape God's punishment. But the children of the righteous will be delivered and kept safe by God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wicked will be punished. The righteous will be delivered.
verses.meaning: No alliance of wickedness — however powerful or popular — can circumvent God's justice. The 'hand join in hand' image suggests organised evil. Yet God's justice is certain. And the righteous — and even their offspring — are under God's protective care.
verses.prayer: God, thank You that justice belongs to You.
verses.discussion_question: Why can we trust God when bad things seem unfair?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children trust in God's ultimate justice when they see wickedness unpunished in the short term — keeping faith without becoming bitter or vengeful?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for one situation in the world or your community where you need to trust God's justice.
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of shadowy figures holding hands surrounded by darkness, but a glowing family in the light protected by divine arms, watercolour contrast illustration

verses.kjv: As a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.
verses.little_bible: A gold ring in a pig's snout looks completely wrong. Beauty without wisdom and careful thinking is just as out of place. Real beauty includes wisdom and godly character.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Beauty without wisdom is wasted.
verses.meaning: This striking image illustrates the absurdity of beauty without wisdom. A gold jewel adorning a pig is grotesque and misplaced — equally out of place is a physically attractive person without discretion (careful, godly thinking and self-control). True beauty includes inward character.
verses.prayer: God, make me wise and beautiful in character.
verses.discussion_question: Why does being wise make a person more beautiful?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children (especially daughters) a higher value for inner beauty and wisdom than for physical appearance and social approval?
verses.do_it_today: Compliment someone today for their character or wisdom — not just their looks.
verses.illustration_prompt: A gold ring gleaming absurdly on a muddy pig's snout in contrast with a girl in simple clothes radiating gentle wisdom and light, watercolour humorous-yet-tender illustration

verses.kjv: The desire of the righteous is only good: but the expectation of the wicked is wrath.
verses.little_bible: What the righteous person wants is only good — their desires are shaped by God. But what the wicked person expects to receive is wrath and judgment. Our desires reveal who we truly are.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteous desires lead to good. Wicked desires lead to wrath.
verses.meaning: The righteous have desires that are aligned with what is good — their wants have been shaped by God. The wicked, however, expect (and will receive) wrath. The contrast is not just about outcomes but about the orientation of the heart — what we desire reveals who we are.
verses.prayer: God, shape my desires to want what is good.
verses.discussion_question: What do you most want? Is it something good?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children have their desires shaped by Scripture and godly community — so that what they want naturally aligns with what is good?
verses.do_it_today: Write down three things you really want. Are they good and God-honouring desires?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child reaching upward toward glowing good things — kindness, truth, love — while a shadowy figure reaches toward crumbling things, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.
verses.little_bible: Some people give generously and keep getting more. Others hold tightly to what they have — and end up with less. This is God's upside-down economy: generosity grows, hoarding shrinks.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Giving generously leads to more. Hoarding leads to less.
verses.meaning: This is one of Scripture's clearest statements of the paradox of generosity. Scattering (generous giving) leads to increase — because God multiplies what is given away. Withholding beyond what is wise leads to poverty — not just materially but often in relationships, community, and soul.
verses.prayer: God, make me a generous giver like You.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever given something away and felt richer?
verses.family_discussion: How do we practise generosity as a family discipline — making it a joyful habit rather than a reluctant obligation, in response to God's own generosity to us?
verses.do_it_today: Give something away today — food, time, money, a kind word — and trust God with the rest.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child scattering seeds with open hands, seeds multiplying as they fall into golden soil, a contrast figure clutching seeds that wither, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
verses.little_bible: The generous person will be richly satisfied — their own soul will be nourished. The one who waters others will themselves be watered. You cannot out-give God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The generous person will be blessed in return.
verses.meaning: The generous person ('liberal soul') is enriched — not necessarily in wealth but in God's blessing and fulfilment. The image of watering and being watered captures the reciprocal nature of generosity: what we give to others returns to us. This is a principle of God's kingdom.
verses.prayer: God, help me water others with Your love.
verses.discussion_question: What happens inside you when you help someone who really needed it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a family culture of generous giving — not calculating return but trusting God's promise that generosity is never lost?
verses.do_it_today: Water someone today: encourage them, help them, serve them. Watch what happens to your own heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child cheerfully watering a plant that grows tall and then droops toward the child to water them in return, happy watercolour garden scene

verses.kjv: He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.
verses.little_bible: The person who hoards grain when people are hungry will be cursed by those around them. But the one who makes food available will be blessed by all. Hoarding in a time of need is cruel.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Sharing in a time of need brings blessing.
verses.meaning: Hoarding food during scarcity to drive up prices was a form of oppression. The community rightly condemns those who exploit scarcity for personal gain. Those who make goods available to those in need receive blessing. This is applied economics shaped by covenant community values.
verses.prayer: God, help me share when others are in need.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wrong to keep things to yourself when others are going without?
verses.family_discussion: How do we respond to scarcity — with hoarding and self-protection, or with generosity and trust in God's provision? What does our reflex reveal about our faith?
verses.do_it_today: Find something in your home to share with someone who needs it more than you do.
verses.illustration_prompt: A generous market seller handing grain to hungry families, a warm community scene with golden light, joyful watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him.
verses.little_bible: The person who keeps looking for ways to do good will find favour with God and people. But whoever keeps looking for trouble will find trouble coming right back at them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Seek good and find favour. Seek mischief and find trouble.
verses.meaning: What we seek determines what we find — and what finds us. Diligent pursuit of good builds favour with God and others. But the search for mischief and wrongdoing brings harm back upon the one seeking it. Our seeking shapes our story.
verses.prayer: God, help me always seek what is good.
verses.discussion_question: What do you spend the most time looking for or thinking about?
verses.family_discussion: How do we shape what our children seek — through the content they consume, the friendships they cultivate, and the habits they build?
verses.do_it_today: Look for one chance to do good today — and take it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a magnifying glass searching for hidden good deeds in a garden, finding glowing flowers, warm sunny watercolour exploration scene

verses.kjv: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.
verses.little_bible: Trusting in money and riches will cause you to fall. But the righteous person will flourish and grow like a healthy, living branch on a tree. God is a better foundation than gold.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Trust in riches and fall. The righteous flourish like a branch.
verses.meaning: Wealth is an unreliable foundation — it cannot hold the weight of a life's trust. Those who put their security in riches will fall when riches fail. But the righteous person flourishes — like a green, fruit-bearing branch connected to a living tree (a picture of connection to God).
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You more than money.
verses.discussion_question: What is one thing money cannot do for you no matter how much you have?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a healthy, non-anxious relationship with money in our home — where it is a tool and not a god, a provision to steward and not a security to trust?
verses.do_it_today: Name three things in your life that money cannot give you. Thank God for each one.
verses.illustration_prompt: A flourishing green branch on a tall tree glowing in sunlight, below it a bag of coins crumbling to dust, watercolour life-vs-riches contrast

verses.kjv: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.
verses.little_bible: A person who causes trouble inside their own family will end up with nothing — only wind to hold. And the fool will end up serving the wise person. What you build in your home matters.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A troublemaker in the family ends up with nothing.
verses.meaning: 'Inheriting wind' is an image of emptiness — gaining nothing after all the trouble caused. Those who sow chaos in their own households will reap nothing lasting. And foolishness leads to servitude — ultimately you serve what is wiser than you. Character determines outcome.
verses.prayer: God, help me build my family, not trouble it.
verses.discussion_question: How can even small things you do or say affect your whole family?
verses.family_discussion: What habits and patterns in our home build it up — and which ones, if left unchecked, could slowly tear it down? How do we address them together?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that builds peace and joy in your home rather than tension or conflict.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child offering a flower to a parent in a warm kitchen scene, a sense of peace and building, while wind blows emptily outside, watercolour cosy home illustration

verses.kjv: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person produces fruit that gives life — like a tree of life to those around them. And the person who cares about others knowing God is truly wise. Share the good news of God with others.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteous people give life to others like a tree.
verses.meaning: Righteousness is not just internally beneficial — it produces life for others. The righteous person is like a tree of life, whose fruit nourishes those around them. And 'winning souls' — leading others to God — is identified as a mark of wisdom. Evangelism is not just duty; it is wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, help me tell others about You.
verses.discussion_question: Who is one person you would like to tell about God?
verses.family_discussion: How do we raise children who see sharing faith as natural wisdom — not awkward obligation — by modelling a life that is genuinely attractive and life-giving to those around it?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one person who does not know God. Pray for them today. Ask God for a chance to share His love.
verses.illustration_prompt: A flourishing tree with golden fruit glowing with life, a child offering fruit to others around them with joy, warm evangelical watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.
verses.little_bible: Even the righteous receive consequences for their actions here on earth. How much more, then, will the wicked and the sinner receive what they deserve! God's justice is real — even now, not just later.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God rewards the righteous and judges the wicked.
verses.meaning: This closing verse is an argument from lesser to greater: if even the righteous receive recompense (reward or consequence) in this life, then certainly the wicked will receive their due — and much more. God's justice is not only eschatological; it is active in history. There is no escape from accountability before God.
verses.prayer: God, help me live knowing You see all things.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter that God sees everything we do?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a healthy, God-fearing reverence for accountability in our children — not anxious fear but a genuine awareness that all of life is lived before God's eyes?
verses.do_it_today: Live today as if God is watching every choice — because He is. Ask Him to help you.
verses.illustration_prompt: An open eye of light in the sky watching over a town, a righteous child below walking confidently, a sinner stumbling in shadow, reverent watercolour scene
